argument_uniqueness_tracing.delivery_plan_id: (1) 659ec7ca-2502-44d4-b67d-e4b9384bb862. (2) The docstring asks for the 'reference number of the patient's delivery plan whose overdue cycle is being paid, as shown by the delivery plan lookup'; find_delivery_plans returned exactly one plan for her, the past-due Kestrel Delivery Pass Annual. (3) She holds no other plan, so every correct agent passes this reference.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.cycle_start_date: (1) 2026-09-08. (2) The docstring: 'first day of the billing cycle this payment covers, written YYYY-MM-DD exactly as the plan record shows its current billing cycle start'; the rule: 'the patient settles the overdue cycle by paying the overdue-cycle settlement for the cycle that began on the plan's current cycle start date'. The plan record shows cycle_start_date 2026-09-08. (3) The earlier cycles (2022-09-08 to 2025-09-08) already carry collected fees and are not overdue, so only 2026-09-08 fits.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.amount_usd: (1) 47.96. (2) Overdue-cycle settlement = subscription fee 48.00 - suspended-day credit + reinstatement fee still due. Suspended-day credit: 4 collected subscription fees (>= long_standing_cycles 3) -> daily method, 48.00 x 6 days past due (2026-09-08 failure not counted, 2026-09-14 counted) / 365 days in the cycle 2026-09-08..2027-09-07 = 0.789 -> 0.79. Reinstatement fee: 6 days past due is at least short_lapse_days 4 and below long_lapse_days 8 -> 2.00. Cap: primary insurance record in active status is a Medicare Part D Enhanced Plan -> 1.50 (the terminated Medicaid record does not count), so the fee is reduced to 1.50. Relief: active Kestrel Care Rewards Gold with 23 completed deliveries in 12 months (>= 8) -> 50 percent, acting on the capped fee -> 0.75. Result 48.00 - 0.79 + 0.75 = 47.96. The cap acts before the relief, as the rule pins down.

user_scenario: You are Loretta Wexford, 69, a retired school librarian in Tukwila, Washington, calling Kestrel Pharmacy's Patient Care Desk from home on a Monday morning. You are courteous and precise, a little worn down by rush deliveries that turn up late, and you would rather get one thing sorted properly than chat. Last Thursday evening, September 10, you had a one-hour rush delivery of your new sleep prescription; the courier could not get into your building the first time, came back, and the bag reached you a little after nine at night, well past the window you had been promised. You are calling because you want the late-delivery refund on that Thursday rush order put through. You have not looked at what, if anything, was charged for it and you know none of the amounts; you just want whatever Kestrel gives back when a rush delivery is late. When the agent asks who you are, you give your phone number, 2065550517, and your date of birth, 1957-03-27; you offer your email, loretta.wexford@fastmail.com, or your home ZIP code, 98188, only if the agent asks for something more. If the agent asks which delivery, you say it was the rush order on the evening of Thursday the 10th with your sleeping pills in it, nothing else in the bag, brought to your home on South 152nd Street as usual. If the agent asks what went wrong, you explain that the gate code of your building had changed so the driver could not get in on the first try, and that when the driver came back you signed and showed your ID at the door. You are happy for the agent to put the refund through for you. If the agent explains that the rush fee for that order still has to be put on your account before anything can come back off it, that is fine with you. If the agent tells you that the yearly payment for your Delivery Pass did not go through and has to be settled first, you are surprised - you did see an email about your card last week but thought it was about something else - and you say you will pay it yourself right now; once the agent hands the payment over to you, you make it with exactly the plan, cycle date and amount the agent gives you, and you tell the agent it went through. You have no paperwork to check the agent's figures against, so you accept the amounts you are given, and you do not raise anything else. When the agent tells you the late-delivery refund on the Thursday order has been booked, you thank them warmly and say goodbye.

design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER - delivery_and_pickup task 0 (Loretta Wexford, Kestrel Delivery Pass Annual, frozen 2026-09-14 11:20 EDT)

[Step 0 - draw] `.venv/bin/python skills/erl-task-instantiate/scripts/draw_counts.py env/env_0021_retail_pharmacy_chain/tasks/delivery_and_pickup --tasks 2` printed: {"task": 0, "prerequisite_problems": 2, "problems": 3, "factor_counts": [4, 4, 6]} and {"task": 1, "prerequisite_problems": 1, "problems": 2, "factor_counts": [6, 4]}. Task 0 therefore has a root plus exactly 2 prerequisite problems, >= max(2-1,1) = 1 value_input edge (both edges are value_input), and factor counts 4 (overdue-cycle settlement), 6 (express order fee), 4 (late-delivery refund).

[Step 0 - scope snapshot] Occupied before this task: nothing (task 0 is first). Claimed here: delivery_ext_overdue_cycle_settlement (target settle_overdue_pass_fee_c99b5804, owner=user), delivery_ext_express_order_fee (charge_order_fee_01b49350, agent), delivery_ext_late_delivery_refund (refund_late_delivery_fee_e6f66314, agent). Reserved headroom for task 1 (1 prerequisite problem, counts [6,4]): the dispatch-cancellation refund (delivery_order_cancelled / refund_reason cancelled_before_dispatch) and the switch of a Delivery Pass (delivery_plan_details_updated + its first subscription charge, owner=user) - both untouched here, both with their own writes, own factors and own customer-owned tool. Lost-package refunds and redelivery orders stay unclaimed and are not needed by task 1.
Blueprint pre-check: base events and policies of delivery close (subscription billing with grace_period time gate, order fees with one_fee_type_per_order, refunds with refund_once + lost_claim_window + trace_complete gating every delivery_fee_refunded write, plan cancellation with no gate). The only patient-owned act the blueprint names is cancelling a plan; a cancellation carries no amount, so the customer-owned write of this task is the patient's own payment of the overdue Delivery Pass cycle (a payment disposing of her own money, the canonical user write of the skill); fee charging and refunding stay agent service actions as the blueprint says.

[Design thesis] Surface goal: "the late-delivery refund on Thursday's rush order". Core scored values: the refund (6.78), which rests on the express fee (8.36), which rests on the overdue cycle being settled (47.96, paid by the patient). Chain: surface goal -> the refund is worked out only after the late order's speed fee stands booked (none is booked: the order was placed while the plan was past due) -> the express fee of a past-due-period order is not fixed until the subscription fee of its cycle stands collected (the 2026-09-08 renewal failed) -> the patient pays the overdue cycle -> fee booked -> refund booked. Depth 3 writes; breadth: cycle ledger, order ledger (23 completions, attempts), 3-month refund history, rx fill history (cross-difficulty), coverage class (cross-difficulty), rewards level.

[Problem-tree card]
Root: delivery_ext_late_delivery_refund (on_request, agent). Edge 1: late_delivery_refund -> express_order_fee, kind value_input, gate fee_booked, form state, sentence (affirmative): "A late-delivery refund is worked out only after the late order's speed fee stands booked on the plan's charge ledger; the fee refunded is that speed fee." Condition: the ledger carries an express_fee entry naming the late order (its speed fee). Resolved by charge_order_fee_01b49350 (agent). False at opening: no delivery_charges row has source_order_id = the 2026-09-10 order (the six fee rows name the 06-09, 06-12, 07-23, 07-28, 08-21, 08-26 orders). Only the express-fee policy's write books an order fee in this difficulty (the settlement books a subscription fee, the refunds book refunds), so the state names exactly one resolving write.
Edge 2: express_order_fee -> overdue_cycle_settlement, kind value_input, gate cycle_fee_collected, form state, sentence (negated direction): "The express fee of an order placed while its plan is past due is not fixed until the subscription fee of the billing cycle in which the order was placed stands collected on the plan's ledger." Condition: a collected subscription entry with cycle_start_date = the plan's current cycle start 2026-09-08. Resolved by settle_overdue_pass_fee_c99b5804 (owner=user). False at opening: delivery_plans.status = past_due, past_due_since = 2026-09-08, cycle_start_date = 2026-09-08, and the newest subscription row is cycle 2025-09-08. The only write that books a subscription fee for the cycle in which a past-due-period order was placed is the overdue settlement (a switch books a new cycle starting on the switch date and is not allowed on a past-due plan).
Four-point test, both sentences: explicit connective ("only after" / "not ... until"); the waited-on side is a record-visible state (fees standing booked on the charge ledger; a subscription fee standing collected on the plan's ledger); no tool, id or snake_case token; strength "only after"/"not until" matches the hard requirement, scope is the late order's fees / the cycle in which the order was placed. Directions differ by business voice: a refund figure "is worked out only after" what it rests on; a charge that waits for standing "is not fixed until" the standing is restored.
Derivation: sentence 2 + plan record (past_due since 2026-09-08, no 2026-09-08 subscription entry) + settlement policy rule ("the patient settles the overdue cycle ... and the payment is booked as that cycle's subscription fee") -> the patient's settlement payment; sentence 1 + order ledger (no fee on the 09-10 order) + express-fee rule -> booking the express fee.
Topological order: settlement -> express fee -> refund (a chain; no parallel edges).
Deletion sensitivity (evalx replay, scratch evaluator using the real tools): skipping the settlement gives express fee 9.06 (discount withheld) and refund 7.34; skipping the fee booking gives refund 0.00. Both edges bear weight.
user_scenario mentions neither prerequisite on its own initiative (only inside conditionals triggered by the agent's explanation); tools validate nothing (each tool reads the plan only to copy customer_id and fees_net_usd, then writes).

[Base-invariant card]
Step 11 settlement - subject delivery_subscription_charged + delivery_plan_recovered; governing base: delivery_evt_subscription_billing. one_charge_per_cycle ("Each cycle is charged once."): authority system record; correlation delivery_plan_id + cycle_start_date = plan 659ec7ca / 2026-09-08; no delivery_subscription_charged row with that cycle start exists before the write. grace_period (time): anchor delivery_plans.past_due_since = 2026-09-08, duration params.past_due_grace_days = 14 (Annual), calendar days with the failure date as day 0, not_after, inclusive -> last day 2026-09-22; frozen 2026-09-14 = day 6 -> satisfied; 2026-09-23 would fail.
Step 13 express fee - subject delivery_order_fee_charged; governing delivery_evt_order_fees. one_fee_type_per_order: no delivery_order_fee_charged row with source_order_id = the 09-10 order and fee_type express_fee. The allowance precondition is inherited verbatim ("The free express allowance itself is counted as the Delivery & Pickup Services charter counts it"): September express orders 09-01, 09-03, 09-05 used the 3 free slots (no express_fee rows), so the 09-10 order is the fourth and is charged.
Step 15 refund - subject delivery_fee_refunded; governing delivery_evt_refunds. refund_once: the fee booked at step 13 (dch_e93ac6e0a711) has no refund. lost_claim_window (time): scheduled 2026-09-10 + 7 calendar days = 2026-09-17 >= 2026-09-14 (inclusive; 2026-09-18 fails). trace_complete (time): scheduled Thu 2026-09-10 + 2 business days = Mon 2026-09-14 <= frozen (inclusive, frozen is exactly the boundary; 2026-09-11 fails). Late test (base handover rule): completed 21:05 vs promised_window_end 19:40 = 85 minutes > late_threshold_minutes 30; late_credit_applies true on the Annual pass.

[Business-object card] Target plan 659ec7ca (Annual). Target order = the 2026-09-10 express order (placed row c260794c...; attempt row building_access; completion 21:05 id_checked_signature). Correlation key: source_order_id. Included in the refund base: only fee rows with source_order_id = that order (the one booked at step 13). Excluded: the four July/August express fees and their four late-delivery refunds (other orders, already settled 6.29 each); September free express orders (no fee). The settlement correlates by cycle_start_date 2026-09-08; the four earlier subscription rows (2022..2025, 48.00 each) settle earlier cycles and only count toward the suspended-day credit tier.

[Factor card - with the Step 5 sensitivity figures (evalx replay on the handling-time world)]
Overdue-cycle settlement (4 factors; baseline "An overdue cycle is settled by collecting the plan's subscription fee for that cycle, rounded to the cent." = 48.00):
- suspended_day_credit (method): 4 collected subscription fees (>= 3) -> daily proration 48.00 x 6 / 365 = 0.79 (weekly tier would give 0 for 6 days; no-credit baseline -> 48.75).
- reinstatement_fee (parameter): 6 days past due in [4,8) -> 2.00 (baseline 0 -> 47.21). Near-miss (round 2): the terminated Medicaid Managed Care record (primary, terminated 2025-12-31) would cap the reinstatement fee at 0.50 and give 47.46; only the primary record in active status counts.
- reinstatement_cap (parameter, cross-difficulty coverage): coverage_plans row = Medicare Part D Enhanced Plan, active -> cap 1.50 (baseline uncapped -> 48.21).
- reinstatement_relief (parameter, multi-source: rewards level AND 12-month completed deliveries): Gold, active AND 23 completions >= 8 -> 50 percent (baseline 0 -> 48.71).
Cap acts before relief (rule: "first reduced to its cap ... the relief percentage then acts on that capped fee"): 1.50 x 50% = 0.75. Result 48.00 - 0.79 + 0.75 = 47.96; all-baseline 48.00.
Express order fee (6 factors; baseline "An express order that the free express allowance does not cover is charged the plan's express fee, rounded to the cent." = 6.99):
- maintenance_delivery_discount (parameter, cross-difficulty rx, multi-source): rx_fills in 6 months up to 2026-09-14: home-delivery pickups 06-11, 07-11, 08-10, 09-10 = 4; refills 04-11, 05-12, 06-11, 07-11, 08-10 = 5 -> tier "at least 3 of both, not both 6" -> 10 percent (baseline 0 -> 9.06). Near-miss: the 2026-03-12 home-delivery pickup is 6 whole months back and falls outside the window, and counter pickups (02-10, 04-11, 05-12) do not count; counting either would still not reach 6 pickups.
- high_value_supplement: value 142.60 -> 1.00 (baseline -> 7.86). long_distance_express_supplement: 11.4 mi > 10 radius, <= 12 -> 1.25 (baseline -> 7.74). id_check_handling_supplement (multi-source): controlled AND no store items -> 1.00 (baseline -> 7.86). evening_express_supplement: window end 19:40 -> 0.90 (baseline -> 7.91).
- plan_age_supplement_adjustment (method): opened 2022-08-09, 49 whole months -> keep 50% rounded down: 4.15 -> 2.07 (baseline keep all -> 10.44).
Speed charge 6.99 x 90% = 6.291 (discount applies only because the cycle fee stands collected after step 11). Result RND(6.291 + 2.07) = 8.36; all-baseline 6.99.
Late-delivery refund (4 factors; baseline "A late order's speed fee is refunded at late_delivery_refund_pct percent of that speed fee, rounded to the cent." = 8.36):
- fault_share (parameter): attempt 1 failed for building_access -> 75 (baseline 100 -> 8.36 after the fee limit).
- late_refund_frequency_share (parameter): 4 late_delivery refunds 07-24, 07-29, 08-22, 08-27 in the 3 months up to today -> >= late_credit_max_per_cycle 4, < 6 -> 80 (baseline -> 8.36). Near-miss (round 2): the late refunds of 2026-06-10 and 2026-06-13 are 3 whole months back; counting them gives 6 -> 50 and a refund of 4.24.
- controlled_handover_share (parameter, multi-source): express AND controlled -> 90 (baseline -> 7.53).
- rewards_refund_adjustment (method): Gold, active -> x150% rounded up to the cent: 4.5144 -> 6.78 (baseline keep as worked -> 4.51).
Shares applied successively to the fee: 8.36 x .75 x .80 x .90 = 4.5144 -> 6.78, limited to 8.36. All-baseline 8.36.
No factor reads a stamp: tiers come from COUNT/SUM/LATEST over the plan's ledgers, DAYS/MONTHS spans, XCOUNT over rx_fills, and CFIELD over coverage_plans / rewards_memberships.
Overrides declared in overwrite (no second product law): subscription billing "a plan ... is charged that fee ..." (the settlement differs from the fee); order fees "An express_1hr order is charged express_1hr_fee_usd, waived while ..." and "Where the plan is past due ...
